texts.preamble: M/S Omkar Agency & Anr vs The State Of Bihar & Ors on 14 October, 2014 Author: Mihir Kumar Jha Bench: Mihir Kumar Jha In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna Civil Writ Jurisdiction Case No.12886 of 2014 ====================================================== M/s Omkar Agency & Anr .... .... Petitio Versus The State of Bihar & Ors .... .... Responde ====================================================== Appearance : For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Prabhat Ranjan, Adv. For the Respondent/s : Mr. P.N.Shahi, Aagx ====================================================== Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Mihir Kumar Jha Oral Order 5 14-10-2014
texts.arguments: 2. The prayer of the petitioners in this writ application reads as follows: "I. The petitioners who are producers within the meaning of Section 3(k) of the COTPA 2003 are out side the scope of applicability of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sales) Regulation 2011 does not operate as a bar for manufacturing, production, marketing, storage etc. of the Scheduled Tobacco Products. II. Petitioners dealing in the production and marketing of Scheduled Tobacco Products within the meaning of Section 3(p) of THE CIGARETTES AND OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS (PROHIBITION OF ADVERTISEMENT AND REGULATION OF TRADE AND COMMERCE, PRODUCTION, SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION) ACT 2003 (hereinafter referred to as COTPA) are not performing a food business and as such are not a food business operator within the meaning of Section 3(n) and 3(a) are consequently not require to submit to the statutory requirements under Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and the Regulations made thereunder; and III. The order dated 21.5.2014 (Annexure 2) issued by respondent no.3 in exercise of powers under section 30(2)(a) is illegal, beyond jurisdiction, unconstitutional and unenforceable." M/S Omkar Agency & Anr vs The State Of Bihar & Ors on 14 October, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31814573/ 1 3. Mr. Prabhat Ranjan, learned counsel for the petitioners, in support of the aforementioned prayer has referred to the various provisions of the Cigarettes & other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as COTPA) and on the basis of analyzing the provisions thereof he is of the view that the subsequent Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 2006 Act) cannot cover Gutka as a food product. According to him the recourse taken by the respondent State of Bihar through its Food Safety Commissioner for banning Gutka is wholly without jurisdiction, inasmuch as Gutka by itself is not covered even in the wide definition of Food under section 3(j) of 2006 Act. Reliance in this regard has also been placed by him on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Godawat Pan Masala Products I.P.Ltd. & anor. V. Union of India & ors., reported in (2004) 7 SCC 68. 4. Mr. P.N.Shahi, learned AAGX, appearing on behalf of the State, on the other hand, has submitted that niceties apart the issue in hand has already been decided by this Court in a judgment dated 10.7.2012 in C.W.J.C.No. 10297/2012 ( Lal Babu Yadav v. the State of Bihar & ors.), wherein an exactly similar notification, of course for an earlier period of one year in terms of Section 30 of 2006 Act after considering the aforesaid judgment of Apex Court in the case of Godawat Pan Masala(supra) has been held to be valid. He would, therefore, submit that this writ application also for the reasons given in the judgment of Lal Babu Yadav (supra) has to meet the similar fate. 5. This Court also must note yet another submission of Mr. Shahi that the same issue is now being directly agitated before the Apex Court in S.L.A.(Civil) No. 16308/2007 in the case of Ankur Gutkha v. Indian Asthama Care Society & ors. wherein large number of cases from different High Courts on the same issue has been transferred and the State of Bihar also proposes to file an application before the Apex Court for transfer of this writ petition to the Apex Court for its being heard together with the case of Ankur Guthka (supra). 6. Mr. Prabhat Ranjan, in reply, has submitted that the aforesaid view taken by the learned Single Judge in the judgment of Lal Babu Yadav (supra) was subsequently noticed by a learned Single Judge of this Court in its order dated 16.1.2013 in C.W.J.C.No. 18782/2012 (Rajat Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. the Union of India & ors.) and its analogous cases who an appreciation of materials on record had referred the matter to the Division Bench for an authoritative pronouncement but unfortunately the matter could not be decided by the Division Bench as the petitioners of Rajat Industries Pvt. Ltd. and its analogous cases (supra) had sought to withdraw their writ applications on account of its becoming infructuous with a leave to file a fresh writ application if there be a fresh cause of action. According to Mr. Prabhat Ranjan the learned Counsel for the petitioner the impugned notification dated 21.5.2014 assailed in this writ application is the fresh cause of action.
